title: Anchored eval scorecard protections for canary/A-B/shadow workflows
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Goal: Implement an anchored (stable-reference) eval scorecard system that gates canary rollouts, A/B tests, and shadow traffic by detecting subtle quality regressions against curated prompt sets. This ticket covers the core evaluation pipeline, signal extraction, gating logic and Console/Alerting hooks needed for automated soft/auto-rollback behavior.

Background: Existing rollout safeguards detect gross regressions (latency, error-rate) but lack sensitive, repeatable checks for semantic quality regressions that show up in production prompts. We need deterministic, low-latency evals built from 'anchored' prompt sets: diverse golden prompts + stratified adversarial samples + per-customer critical prompts.

Scope:
- Define anchor scorecard schema (per-prompt expected outputs, metric suite, weighting).
- Implement batched evaluation runner that can score new model binaries against the anchored reference in < 10s for typical canary sizes.
- Compute statistical deltas: per-metric delta, Holm-Bonferroni adjusted p-values, and a composite regression score.
- Integrate with rollout controller: block canaries when composite regression > threshold OR when any critical prompt drops below threshold.
- Shadow/A-B integration: surface paired-difference test on shadow traffic (paired by request id) and run online bootstrap to estimate confidence.
- Auto-rollback policy: configurable in Console with modes (soft-alert, pause & hold, immediate rollback).
- Console UI: scorecard diff view, per-prompt examples, and one-click investigate (link to failed examples + reproduce runner).
- Telemetry: store raw scoring traces, per-request hashes, and eval-run metadata for audits.

Non-goals: full auto-remediation (model retrain) and heavy-weight offline eval pipelines (those are separate).

Acceptance criteria:
1) New scorecard schema checked into model-lifecycle repo and validated by unit tests.
2) End-to-end test: create a canary job that runs anchored evals and fails the canary for an injected regression in 95% of runs.
3) Console shows scorecard diffs and allows toggling rollback mode.
4) Metrics emitted: eval_run.duration_ms, eval.composite_delta, eval.critical_prompt_fail_count; alerts wired to PagerDuty for P0 regressions.

Risks & Trade-offs:
- False positives vs sensitivity: too-sensitive gating will increase manual interventions. We will expose conservative defaults and per-customer hysteresis.
- Eval runtime cost: running full golden set on every canary is expensive; we plan fast-path sampling and prioritized prompt early-exit heuristics.

Open questions for design/PM:
- Default composite weighting across metrics (BLEU/ROUGE improved? prefer embedding similarity + human-calibrated thresholds).
- Per-tenant thresholds and SLAs: should Paid Enterprise get looser/harder gates?

comments: 2026-03-02 - Priya Shah: Kickoff meeting notes. Agreed on 3-tier prompt sets: (1) core golden (100 examples), (2) adversarial (50), (3) customer-critical (variable). Action: Marco to prototype runner against runtime-1.20 models.

2026-03-04 - Marco Reyes: Prototype complete. Runner can evaluate the 150-example anchored set in ~6.4s on a dedicated batch instance using KV-cache warm path. Observed flakiness for stochastic sampling; adding deterministic seeds improved stability.

2026-03-06 - Elena Kuznetsova (QA): Found edge-case where temperature sampling produced nondeterministic match rates even with fixed seeds due to non-deterministic kernel ordering on some GPU types. Proposed solution: run with greedy/beam for gating-critical prompts and fall back to sampling-only in non-blocking metrics.

2026-03-07 - Marco Reyes: Implemented per-prompt execution mode (deterministic / stochastic) and an early-exit when a critical prompt fails hard threshold. Updated unit-tests and added a synthetic regression test (injects token-drop).

2026-03-09 - Priya Shah: PM review: request adding Console controls for per-project threshold overrides and a noise-hysteresis knob to avoid rollbacks on transient spikes. Also request Audit fields for who changed thresholds.

2026-03-11 - Marco Reyes: Wiring alerts: eval.composite_delta > 0.12 triggers P0 path. Integrated with rollout controller so that if a canary is blocked, the rollout pauses and posts links to failing prompts. Created initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-lifecycle/pull/487

2026-03-12 - Security (L. Huang): Quick review: eval traces contain customer prompts; ensure traces sent to telemetry are redacted or only hashed unless customer opted-in. Added security_review_required=true to ticket.
2026-03-12 - Marco Reyes: Updated pipeline to store only salted SHA256 of prompt text in telemetry by default and to keep raw examples in per-customer encrypted buckets when allowed by config.
playbook: If a P0 anchored-eval alert fires: (1) Rollout controller pauses new canaries; (2) Ops triage: inspect Console scorecard diffs; (3) Reproduce with runner using same seed; (4) If regression confirmed, toggle auto-rollback (immediate) or revert canary model; (5) Postmortem required for > 30% critical prompt failure.
investigation_steps: Fetch failing examples from Console -> scorecard diff
Run local reproduce runner with deterministic seed
Check model version differences and commit-range in GitHub
notes: We will ship conservative defaults first: composite threshold 0.12, critical prompt pass-rate >= 92%, sampling mode: greedy for gating. Enterprise customers may opt to disable auto-rollback and receive advisory alerts instead.
